attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his Where's Your Ed At post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps both categorical negatives: no trillion-dollar problems solved and no profitable outcomes for any business. The claim is firm and unhedged, so it is a present-tense observation that can be scored.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: a profitable outcome means attributable benefits exceed costs for some business, achieved by the post date. The result depends on readings the speaker did not supply: whether AI vendors count as 'any particular business', and what basis is used to judge profit.

evidence.note: A 2022 founder interview says Midjourney was already profitable. That cuts against the blanket negative, but it is the company's own undefined claim with no financials, so it does not meet the cost-coverage requirement.
An IDC survey sponsored by Microsoft reports respondents' own estimates of ROI. These are not realized, fully costed net gains for a named deployment.

Klarna's company disclosure credits AI with part of its efficiency and profit gains. The assistant savings are annualized and forward-looking, and realized net gains from generative AI are not separated out.
Randomized experiments run before the post found gross sales gains. The authors say they cannot estimate ROI because full costs are missing.

reviews.rationale: The packet points against the blanket claim: Midjourney says it is profitable, IDC respondents estimate ROI, Klarna reports AI-driven efficiency, and experiments show sales gains. But no item shows a realized, fully costed net gain from generative AI as the contract requires. Midjourney's undefined self-report also depends on counting AI vendors as qualifying businesses. Nothing establishes either negative, and no verified trillion-dollar solution appears. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.
